'''Maria Antònia Canals''' (15 November 1930 – 29 April 2022)<ref>[https://elpais.com/espana/catalunya/2022-04-30/muere-la-pedagoga-maria-antonia-canals-a-los-91-anos.html Muere la pedagoga Maria Antonia Canals a los 91 años] {{in lang|es}}</ref> was a Spanish mathematician. Her work in [[recreational mathematics]] served as the basis for the eponymous Canals Project. Among other honors, she has been awarded the [[Creu de Sant Jordi]] and the {{ill|Medal of Honor of Barcelona|ca|Medalla d'Honor de Barcelona}}.
{{TOC limit|2}}

==Biography==
María Antònia Canals completed her teaching studies in 1950, and three years later earned a [[Licentiate (degree)#Spain|licentiate]] in exact sciences at the [[University of Barcelona]]. She began working at the [[Lycée Français de Barcelone|Lycée Français]] and at the Talitha School. From 1956 to 1962, she implemented a method of pedagogical renewal in early childhood education, following the [[Montessori education|Montessori model]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NAiIDwAAQBAJ&pg=PT116 |title=Maria Antònia Canals i Tolosa: Renovación pedagógica y didáctica de las matemáticas |trans-title=Maria Antònia Canals i Tolosa: Pedagogical Renewal and Teaching of Mathematics |first=María |last=Sotos Serrano |publisher=Ediciones Octaedro |isbn=9788499218304 |language=Spanish |date=2017-02-10 |access-date=2019-07-31 |via=Google Books}}</ref> As part of that task, she devoted herself to the creation of all necessary materials in the field of [[mathematical game]]s.

In October 1962 she founded the Ton i Guida school, working in an area of Barcelona with a need for greater attention, with students who were immigrants and had very poor living conditions. Its techniques differed from those of most schools in [[Francoist Spain]], more closely resembling ones from the [[Second Spanish Republic|Second Republic]], and classes were taught in [[Catalan language|Catalan]] rather than [[Spanish language|Spanish]]. The endeavor got off to a difficult start, especially in regard to financing, but between 1972 and 1975 it had more than 400 students and was considered a model school.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.barcelona.cat/infobarcelona/en/my-new-post-9949_114969.html |title=The spirit of a 1960s pioneering school in Roquetes |publisher=Nou Barris TV |date=2014-12-01 |access-date=2019-07-31}}</ref> Canals was also the creator and member of various associations of teachers and professors, including the "Perímetre" teacher's group. She taught mathematics education at the [[Autonomous University of Barcelona]] and the Escola de Mestres de Vic.<ref name=alentar>{{Cite web |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/vida/20131223/54398512672/maria-antonia-canals-83-anos-alentar-maestros.html |title=Maria Antònia Canals, 83 años: 'Sigo para alentar a los maestros' |trans-title=Maria Antònia Canals, Age 83: 'I Continue to Encourage Teachers' |first=Bàrbara |last=Julbe |work=[[La Vanguardia]] |language=Spanish |date=2013-12-23 |access-date=2019-07-31}}</ref>

She retired on 30 September 2001, but had continued to work in education. She was named a [[professor emeritus]] at the [[University of Girona]], and remained active in its Gabinet de Materials i de Recerca per a la Matemàtica a l'Escola (GAMAR) research center.<ref name=alentar/>

==Canals Project==
An undertaking of the Descartes Network, the Canals Project ({{langx|es|Proyecto Canals|links=no}}) attempts to [[Digitization|digitize]] the large amount of educational materials created by María Antònia Canals. Emphasis is placed on the use of [[information and communications technology]] and how to integrate it with didactic tools.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://proyectodescartes.org/descartescms/index.php/blog/difusion/item/877-proyecto-canals-inmersion-digital-de-los-materiales-de-maria-antonia-canals/ |title=Proyecto Canals: inmersión digital de los materiales de Maria Antònia Canals |trans-title=Canals Project: Digital Immersion With Materials By Maria Antònia Canals |first=José Antonio |last=Salgueiro |publisher=Descartes Network |language=Spanish |date=2014-07-19 |access-date=2019-07-31}}</ref>
